text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Quasi-governmental Jewish Agency formulates plan to bring new immigrants from the West to beef up Jewish settlements.
- Former KGB station chief in Israel defected in 1988 and betrayed Soviet agents.
- Shin Bet security service angry that police lowered suicide alert level too hastily.
MAARIV
- Suicide bombing warnings and alert continue.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu plans ski vacation in Aspen, Colorado next weekend.
- Hebron massacre gunman Goldstein's gravesite well-tended, surrounded by gardens.
- Netanyahu: Tensions with Syria decrease.
- Finance Minister Meridor says any initiated shekel devaluation will lead to higher inflation and won't help employers.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Argument in Israeli security establishment over level of suicide bomb alert.
GLOBES
- Decline in tax revenues continues.
- Sharp increase in marketing of land by Housing Ministry and Land Administration in September and October.
- Meridor asks parliamentary committee for permission to transfer 45 million shekels from immigration budget to fund construction of 200 housing units for Jewish settlers in the West Bank and Gaza.
JERUSALEM POST
- Syrian President Assad to United States: I will try to block terror.
- New information enables pinpoint security checks.
- Orient House issue keeps EU troika away.
- January-October tax revenues 2 billion shekels short of Treasury's forecast.
